answer: Among black females (race='black', sex='female'; n=1,548 in `data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv`), the largest increase in median composite wealth occurred between 1985 and 1990: the median of composite_wealth_1985 was $175, which rose to $2,600 in composite_wealth_1990 — a raw-dollar absolute Δmedian of +$2,425 (≈+1,386%; ≈+$485 per year over the 5-year span). This exceeds the runner-up interval 1990 → 1996, in which composite_wealth_1990 = $2,600 rose to composite_wealth_1996 = $4,000 (Δmedian = +$1,400; ≈+54%; ≈+$233 per year over the 6-year span). Therefore the largest jump in median wealth for black females is between 1985 and 1990, with 1990 → 1996 the smaller increase.

payload.workflow:
Dataset: `data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv` (12,013 rows × 6 cols; 0 missing on all wealth columns; balanced panel).

Subgroup: race == "black" AND sex == "female" → n = 1,548. (The race token in the file is spelled `hipanic` for hispanics; the BF subset is unaffected.)

Variables (exact names, matching `datasets.json`): composite_wealth_1985, composite_wealth_1990, composite_wealth_1996.

Units: raw U.S. dollars. NO CPI adjustment applied. NO log transform. NO /1000. NO winsorization on headline.

Operational guardrails (per approved plan):
  • Negative composite_wealth values (≈7.6% / 7.4% / 6.5% of BF in 1985/1990/1996) retained as substantive net liabilities, not dropped or zero-imputed.
  • Zeros (≈39.9% / 29.4% / 31.7%) retained as substantive zero-wealth observations.
  • Headline = cross-sectional median at each wave (NOT paired); paired within-person deltas reported as sensitivity only.
  • "Largest increase" = raw-dollar absolute change in cross-sectional median between consecutive waves (most literal reading; not brittle to the tiny $175 1985 base).

=== HEADLINE NUMBERS (cross-sectional, all 1,548 BF rows) ===
  composite_wealth_1985   → median = $175     (n=1,548)
  composite_wealth_1990   → median = $2,600   (n=1,548)
  composite_wealth_1996   → median = $4,000   (n=1,548)

Intervals (Δmedian, raw $):
  1985 → 1990 (5 years) : $175 → $2,600 = +$2,425
                        pct = +1,385.7%;     annualized $/yr = +$485.00
  1990 → 1996 (6 years) : $2,600 → $4,000 = +$1,400
                        pct = +53.8%;        annualized $/yr = +$233.33

INTERVAL-ASYNMMETRY NOTE: 1985→1990 is 5 years while 1990→1996 is 6 years. The headline (raw-$ delta) does not depend on span length. All annualized ahead check that 1985→1990 still wins by ~2× on a per-year basis, consistent with the headline.

=== WINNER (raw-$ absolute Δmedian) ===
  Winner    : 1985 → 1990,  Δmedian = +$2,425
  Runner-up : 1990 → 1996,  Δmedian = +$1,400
  → The largest increase in median composite wealth for black females is between 1985 and 1990.

=== SENSITIVITY APPENDIX ===
(a) % change in cross-sectional median:  1985→1990 = +1,385.7%;   1990→1996 = +53.8%    → agrees with headline ✓
(b) Annualized $/yr cross-sectional:     1985→1990 = +$485/yr;    1990→1996 = +$233/yr   → agrees with headline ✓
(c) Paired within-person median Δ over matched BF panel:
      1985→1990 median of (w_1990 - w_1985) = +$1,000; mean = +$13,849
      1990→1996 median of (w_1996 - w_1990) = +$0   ; mean = +$18,196
    → agrees with headline ✓ (and the median-person DELTA between 1990 and 1996 is exactly $0, indicating half the BF subgroup lost or had flat absolute wealth in the later interval)
(d) Median restricted to nonzero BF rows:
      1985 (nonzero) = $3,832;  1990 (nonzero) = $8,100;  Δ = +$4,268
      1990 (nonzero) = $8,100;  1996 (nonzero) = $19,800; Δ = +$11,700
    → ⚠ FLIPS ranking: among nonzero-wealth BF, 1990→1996 shows the larger raw-$ jump (+$11,700 vs +$4,268). This is NOT promoted to headline because the agreed guardrails retain zeros as substantive, and the flipping-percentage interpretation is biased (excluding the zero mass drops the largest source of late-period downward pressure on the cross-sectional median).
    ⚠ SURFACED PER INSTRUCTION: this reversal is consistent with the share-zero moving from 39.9% (1985) to 29.4% (1990) — i.e., ~10.5 pp of BF respondents exited zero-wealth status between 1985 and 1990, lifting the all-rows median mechanically — and then share-zero edging UP from 29.4% to 31.7% between 1990 and 1996, which is why the all-rows median only advances by $1,400 in the later interval even though those who remained nonzero grew much faster. The headline metric honors the agreed treatment of zero-wealth observations.

=== MEAN / IQR / DISTS (context, not used for ranking) ===
  1985: mean $10,647; IQR $5,000; p90 $18,530; min -$45,922; max $2,403,336; share_zero 39.9%; share_neg 7.6%
  1990: mean $24,496; IQR $16,050; p90 $73,560; min -$71,147; max $1,680,099; share_zero 29.4%; share_neg 7.4%
  1996: mean $42,692; IQR $42,513; p90 $134,180; min -$94,981; max $1,701,683; share_zero 31.7%; share_neg 6.5%
  (Right-skewed; means ≫ medians; means not reliable as a change statistic.)

=== AGREEMENT TABLE ===
  Headline raw-$ cross-sectional Δmedian ........... 1985→1990 winner
  (a) % change cross-sectional median ............... agrees
  (b) annualized $/yr cross-sectional ................ agrees
  (c) paired within-person median of differences ... agrees
  (d) median on nonzero-only rows .................... DISAGREES (1990→1996 wins)
  → 4 of 5 metrics agree on 1985→1990 as the larger jump in median wealth.
